title: Ultimate Information Rate for Quantum Sensing under Multilevel Relaxation
authors: Changhun Oh, Seok Hyung Lie, Youngrong Lim
abstract: We determine the ultimate information rate of a relaxing multilevel quantum sensor under unrestricted adaptive control and construct an explicit strategy that attains it. We consider sensing a weak field that couples the ground state to several excited states that decay back to the ground state, a setting that reduces to amplitude-damping sensing for a single excited state. We show that the ultimate information rate is exactly the mean population lifetime of the bright state coupled to the ground state by the signal. Although the sensing dynamics generally involve several decay modes, an explicit rank-one protocol that monitors the ground--bright coherence using fresh meters and classical feedback attains this rate while keeping its finite-time information deficit bounded by a constant. For independently relaxing identical sensors, independent local monitoring attains the sum of their individual optimal rates, so intersensor entanglement and joint quantum error correction cannot increase the asymptotic rate. Consequently, the free population-decay curve provides an operational measure of the optimal sensing performance under arbitrary adaptive control.
summary: This paper establishes the theoretical limit for quantum sensing in multilevel systems subject to relaxation, proving that the ultimate information rate equals the bright state's mean population lifetime. They construct an explicit, simple monitoring protocol that achieves this rate asymptotically, demonstrating that entanglement cannot improve the rate beyond the sum of independent local rates.
main_problem: The paper determines the ultimate rate at which information can be extracted from a quantum sensor undergoing multilevel relaxation, especially when using unrestricted adaptive control.
main_result: The ultimate information rate is found to be exactly equal to the mean population lifetime of the bright state coupled by the signal. This rate can be achieved asymptotically using a simple rank-one monitoring and feedback protocol.
method: The authors derive the ultimate bound using the Channel-Extension (CE) bound and then construct an explicit, rank-one monitoring protocol that saturates this bound asymptotically.
model_or_system: The system is a multilevel quantum sensor with a ground state and an excited manifold. Sensing involves a weak field coupling the ground state to the excited manifold, while relaxation is governed by a master equation involving multiple decay modes.
key_observables: Ultimate Information Rate ($R$), Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), and the mean population lifetime ($	au_b$).
important_parameters: The relaxation geometry, characterized by the positive operator $G$, and the coupling strength of the weak signal.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes independent local relaxation for multiple sensors and relies on the existence of an optimal rank-one monitoring strategy.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical model, the optimal control protocol involving weak monitoring and feedback, and comparisons between the ultimate bound, free evolution, and the achieved rate for multiple sensors.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical upper bound (CE bound) to deriving the rate-optimal response, and finally constructing a physical, rank-one monitoring protocol that achieves this bound asymptotically.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental benchmark for quantum sensing in realistic, dissipative environments, showing how the intrinsic relaxation dynamics dictate the ultimate measurement precision, even with advanced adaptive control.
